name: Nesingwary's Expedition
summary: Hunters gather at Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale, north of Lake Nazferiti. Hemet Nesingwary has made this camp a base for hunters who test themselves against the jungle's fiercest predators.

sections.title: A Hunters' Outpost in the Jungle
sections.body: Beside the river north of Lake Nazferiti, Nesingwary's Expedition is a hunters' camp founded by Hemet Nesingwary. Sir S. J. Erlgadin, Ajeck Rouack, and Barnil Stonepot are among its seasoned hunters. Hired marksmen guard the camp, while neutral vendors supply it. Skilled riflemen and bowmen of any allegiance are welcome to hunt the jungle's deadliest predators.

sections.title: Pages and Predators
sections.body: At Nesingwary's Expedition, hunters trade competition and tall tales. They learn to track panthers, raptors, and tigers before turning to the jungle's greatest beasts. There is work for scholars, too. Pages from Nesingwary's long manuscript have scattered across the wilds, and the scholars at camp seek every missing chapter.

faq.answer: Hemet Nesingwary, the famed dwarven big game hunter, founded the camp and leads it with a circle of veteran marksmen.

faq.q: Why is the expedition here in Stranglethorn Vale?
faq.answer: The expedition came to Stranglethorn to hunt its dangerous wildlife, from prowling panthers and aggressive raptors to ferocious tigers and legendary trophy beasts.

faq.q: Is Nesingwary's Expedition friendly to both Alliance and Horde?
faq.answer: Yes. Nesingwary's hired guns keep the camp neutral and maintain peace while visitors respect its grounds. Alliance and Horde hunters are welcome to test their tracking skills.

faq.q: What is the story behind the missing manuscript pages?
faq.answer: Hemet Nesingwary wrote an extensive hunting memoir titled 'The Green Hills of Stranglethorn.' Its loose pages were lost in the wilderness, and camp archivist Barnil Stonepot enlisted travelers to recover them.

angles.text: As a hunter, you can hone your tracking skills here against Stranglethorn Vale's deadliest predators.
As a dwarf, you may recognize Hemet Nesingwary and fellow Khaz Modan mountaineers in this humid tropical wild. Grit and a love of the hunt brought them here.
